name: Alpha Centauri
tagline: The nearest star system — a Sun-like binary circled at a distance by Proxima.
history: Alpha Centauri is actually three stars: Alpha Centauri A and B — a Sun-like yellow and an orange dwarf locked in a 80-year binary dance — plus the faint red dwarf Proxima orbiting the pair hundreds of times farther out. To southern sky-watchers it is the third-brightest star and the pointer to the Southern Cross; invisible from most northern latitudes. Its proximity makes it the prime target of interstellar mission concepts like Breakthrough Starshot, which proposes laser-pushed nanocraft crossing the gulf in twenty years. H.G. Wells was among the first to send fictional travelers there, in 1897.
source: IAU; ESO; Yale Bright Star Catalogue
